lots.what_it_is: Tub of games (Gowans: 'TUB OF ASST PC & NINTENDO GAMES CONTROLLERS ETC'). Two loose Australian PAL N64 carts, Banjo-Kazooie (NUS-NBKP-AUS) and Pilotwings 64 (NUS-NPWP-AUS), plus the gold edge of what may be a third cart under Pilotwings. Two grey N64-style controllers (look official, not confirmed), a blue N64-style controller with an OFF/ON switch (so third-party, not Nintendo), cables, a boxed EA Sports PC game, and about 9 PC and PS2 games (The Sims 3, Hitman 2, Torino 2006, Hotel Giant, Tony Hawk's Underground 1 and 2, RollerCoaster Tycoon 2, The Movies, Sims 2 Open for Business).

lots.guide_summary: All 14 surviving entries are SOLD (0 unsold, 0 asking), and they are for parts of the lot, not the whole tub: Banjo-Kazooie loose cart A$19 to A$48 (A$19 to A$25 untested, A$39 to A$48 cleaned and tested), Pilotwings 64 A$7 to A$26, official grey controller A$12 to A$25 each. Taken together, the identified parts would resell for roughly A$60 to A$110 if sold one by one. The PC and PS2 games and the blue third-party controller are not priced (low value, unsourced). Rate 1 USD = 1.4383 AUD. The PriceCharting loose average (US$24.60 for Banjo) was used only as a cross-check.
lots.working: Rate 1 USD = 1.4383 AUD. KEEP: lowest same-condition SOLD for each confirmed cart: Banjo US$13.48 = A$19.39, Pilotwings US$4.58 = A$6.59, total A$25.98 / 1.198 = A$21.69, rounded down to $20. Grey controllers left out of KEEP because I could not confirm they are official. FLIP: likely resale untested Banjo about A$22 (middle of A$19.39, A$21.57, A$25.03), Pilotwings about A$14, two grey controllers at a discounted A$18 each = A$36, total A$72. Less eBay AU fees about 13% = A$62.64, less about A$8 for packing and postage shortfall over 3 to 4 parcels = A$54.64. Divide by 2.396 = A$22.80, rounded down to $20. The PC and PS2 games are counted at nil. Pickup from Moonah, inbound freight $0. Lot already had 9 bids when the page was fetched, so it may well go past $20.
lots.confidence_reason: Both cart labels read and multiple SOLD entries on an opened page, but these are eBay sales gathered by PriceCharting (retail audience, single condition notes only), the carts are untested, and the controllers may not be official.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: researcher entry 2, the PriceCharting 'loose' average US$24.60. It is a computed average, not a price paid, so it is not SOLD evidence. Kept as a cross-check only. Researcher entries 1 and 3 were ranges bundling several sales. I split them into individual dated SOLD entries after checking each on the page (all prices and dates matched). I left out the US$14.32 (with manual), US$11.26 (with players guide) and US$17.58 (German listing, unspecified) sales, which are not the same configuration. Researcher's assumed 1.50 rate replaced with 1.4383 looked up live. Corrections: the second cart is Pilotwings 64, not a racing game. The blue controller is third-party (it has an OFF/ON switch).
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo. Banjo-Kazooie label NUS-NBKP-AUS with Nintendo Seal of Quality, some grime and label wear. Pilotwings 64 label NUS-NPWP-AUS. A third cart edge (contacts) sits under Pilotwings, unidentified. Two grey controllers with official-looking shape. The blue controller with yellow C-buttons has a red OFF/ON switch, so it is third-party. Boxed EA Sports PC game with a $59.95 sticker.
lots.condition: Used, untested. Cart labels have light wear and grime. Controller stick condition unknown.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there a third N64 cartridge under the Pilotwings cart, and what is it? Are the grey controllers marked Nintendo on the back (official), and are the sticks firm? Is there any N64 console or Rumble/Controller Pak in the tub?

lots.what_it_is: Gowans title 'FRAMED BEATTIE PRINT - PORT OF HOBART'. A large sepia panoramic photograph of Hobart and Mt Wellington from the eastern shore, with several warships at anchor in the Derwent. Ribbed walnut-stained frame with gilt slip, grey mount and a caption plate 'PORT OF HOBART'. The Beattie attribution comes from Gowans' title only. A faint white scratched or lettered line at the lower left of the print may be a negative caption or number, but it cannot be read through the glare. It could be an original period print or a later copy.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. The researcher had no entries, the WebSearch budget is used up, and direct searches on Invaluable, Leonard Joel, Colville and LiveAuctioneers returned nothing usable (client-rendered pages or no results).
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so no maximum bid (0 for both).
lots.confidence_reason: No evidence of any kind. The photographer credit is not readable, and original or reproduction cannot be told from one glare-filled photo.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo through glass with heavy glare. Sepia panorama roughly 3:1, in about a 1 m wide frame. Warships visible mid-river. Possible white lettering at the lower left edge of the print, not legible at this resolution. No visible signature, stamp or number.
lots.condition: Frame looks sound. The print looks evenly toned. Foxing or fading cannot be judged through the glare.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you read the lettering at the lower left of the print (for example 'Beattie Photo Hobart' and a number)? Is it an original photograph (silver gelatin, with fine detail under a loupe) or a printed or photocopy reproduction? Is there a label on the back, and what are the sight size and the condition (foxing, tears)?

lots.what_it_is: Washburn KC-40V electric guitar (headstock 'Washburn', truss cover 'KC-40V', both read). Black body with a yellow marbled graphic finish, HSS pickups (two single coils and a bridge humbucker, not HSH as the researcher said), double-locking tremolo with locking nut, rosewood board with dot inlays, two knobs and a selector. Probably a Washburn Chicago Series model from about 1989 to 1992 made in Asia. Year and country are not confirmed (no neck plate photo).
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. The WebSearch budget is used up. Reverb returns HTTP 403 (also to WebFetch), and Grays and LiveAuctioneers searches had nothing usable. My sense is that these usually sell used for a few hundred dollars, but that is unverified and not used.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so no maximum bid (0 for both).
lots.confidence_reason: Model read clearly, but no market evidence at all, and playing condition is unknown.
lots.dropped_entries: None (researcher returned no entries). Correction: the pickup layout is HSS, not HSH.
lots.key_photo_findings: Two photos. The headstock reads Washburn with KC-40V on the truss cover. Strings fitted. Locking nut with three clamps. Tremolo arm fitted. Finish glossy with no obvious large chips in the photos. Back and neck plate not shown.
lots.condition: Looks complete and strung. Electronics, frets and tremolo function untested.
lots.question_for_gowans: Does it play through an amp with all pickups working? Does the tremolo sit level, and are the locking nut clamps and allen keys present? Is there a case or gig bag? What is the serial or country on the neck plate or headstock back?
